title: Revenue Accounting Basis for the No-Show Penalty on the Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
This basis states how Revenue Accounting arrives at the sum withheld from an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking as its no-show penalty.

## 1. The quantities that enter

1.1 **The brand's penalty.** The fare brand's own no-show penalty, as scheduled for the brand the booking is held in.
1.2 **The travellers counted.** The travellers ticketed on the booking, as the booking record carries them.
1.3 **The share withheld.** The whole of the brand's penalty is withheld: the share is 1.
1.4 **The value the ticket still carries.** The fare, tax, service and optional-extra lines standing on the booking, taken together.

## 2. The basis

The no-show penalty withheld from a booking is the fare brand's own no-show penalty, taken once for every traveller ticketed on the booking. The brand's penalty, the travellers counted and the share withheld are multiplied together into the gross penalty, and what the traveller has already paid in reworking the ticket is then taken off that gross figure, never off the brand's penalty before it is multiplied out. Nothing is taken off that gross figure for earlier reworking of the ticket. The figure never falls below zero. The sum withheld is then carried to the cent.

The sum withheld is limited to the value the ticket still carries, read as the fare, tax, service and optional-extra lines standing on the booking, and the result is rounded to the nearest cent.

## 3. The order the operations take

| Step | What is done | What it acts on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the brand's penalty, the travellers counted and the share withheld are multiplied together | the three quantities in section 1 |
| 2 | what has already been paid in reworking the ticket is taken off | the gross penalty of step 1, never the brand's penalty before it was multiplied out |
| 3 | the figure is held at nothing where step 2 would take it lower | the result of step 2 |
| 4 | the figure is carried to the cent | the result of step 3 |
| 5 | the figure is held down to the value the ticket still carries and rounded to the nearest cent | the result of step 4 |

## 4. Worked figure, on hypothetical inputs

Take a booking held in a brand whose scheduled no-show penalty is 150.00 USD, with 2 travellers ticketed, carrying fare and optional-extra lines coming to 1440.00 USD.

The brand's penalty of 150.00 USD, the 2 travellers counted and the share of 1 multiply out to a gross penalty of 300.00 USD. Nothing is taken off for earlier reworking, so the figure stands at 300.00 USD; it is above nothing, and carried to the cent it is 300.00 USD. The value the ticket still carries is 1440.00 USD, which is the larger of the two, so the sum withheld stands at 300.00 USD.

Take the same booking with fare and optional-extra lines coming to 210.00 USD instead. The first four steps give 300.00 USD as before, but the value the ticket still carries is now 210.00 USD, the smaller of the two, so the sum withheld is 210.00 USD.
